main_text.l: Dissolvitur unumquodque eo modo, quo ligatum est 560,3
Dominorum interest, ne servis, contra famem, sævitiam, injuriam juste deprecantibus, denegetur auxilium 57,11
quod uni ex Dominis acquiri non potest aliis per servum acquitur 477,6
*non sunt Domini mature rebus suis defraudandi 210,2
Dominio temere privari, nemo debet rer. suarum 223,7
Dominium rei venditæ manet penes venditorem usque ad traditionem 523,9
Domini jure gentium in servos habent jus vitæ & necis. 57,4
Dominus per servum naturaliter tenentem, civiliter possidet 232,7
Dominus sit non est dubitandum qui non solum operam dedit sed & partem materiæ præstitit 282,25
inter Dominum, & servum nulla obligatio nasci potest 691,3
Donatio mortis causa equi paratur legato. 218,2
Donatio revocatur per pœnitentiam mortis causa 218,3
Dotis causa civile dominium ad maritum transfert. 223,2

page.notes: The left column is cut off at the left edge of the scan, so the first letters of most left-column lines are illegible and marked as such. Entries in the left column that could not be read with certainty are marked [?]. The number 57,4 sits on its own line between two entries; I have attached it to the line above. The lines of the left column are listed in the order of the column, followed by the right column. The shelf-mark and digitiser credit at the bottom are not transcribed.
